question: Which of the following was used as a highway for foreign trade between India and Britain, as its opening in 1869 reduced the cost of transportation and made access to the Indian market easier?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Suez Canal**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, was a major engineering feat that connected the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea, cutting through the Isthmus of Suez in Egypt.
 
• Before its opening, ships traveling between Europe and Asia had to sail around the southern tip of Africa, which was a much longer and more dangerous journey.
 
• The Suez Canal drastically reduced the distance between Europe (particularly Britain) and India, saving about 5,000 miles of travel compared to the previous route around the
 
• This significantly decreased travel time, from several months to about 2-3 weeks.
 
• With the shorter route, the cost of shipping goods decreased.
 
 
• This made it economically feasible to transport bulk goods such as cotton, spices, and tea from India to Britain and vice versa, boosting trade between the two nations.
 
 
 
• The Canal made it much easier for British merchants and traders to access the Indian market.
 
 
• This was vital during the colonial period when Britain was heavily invested in trade with its colonies, including India, which was considered the "jewel in the crown" of the British Empire.
 
 
 
• The Suez Canal's opening also had geopolitical importance.
 
 
• It gave Britain greater control over its colonial empire and facilitated the movement of naval fleets and military forces in the region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
In contrast, the Panama Canal (opened in 1914) connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, the Corinth Canal (opened in 1893) connects the Aegean Sea to the Ionian Sea in Greece, and the White Sea-Baltic Sea Canal (opened in 1933) connects the White Sea in the Arctic to the Baltic Sea
